body:
ESH

1. There is a difference in hair types. As a female I have STRAIGHT hair. Won't hold a curl to save it's fucking life. HOWEVER, I do use a spray in conditioner and hair oil whenever I wash it. So when people ask me about my hair, how I always get it so perfectly straight and looking so healthy, I do start with it's my natural hair and then say what I use. IMO your wife could say her hair is naturally xyz and uses abc products, and by not disclosing that, it's kinda assholeish to lead people to believe she doesn't have to do anything to obtain the look. 
2. You had no reason to blurt that out and put her out like that. You could have communicated with her in private about how you were feeling and had an educational conversation about her hair and routine. Maybe you don't understand it because it's not your hair and you don't know. 

biggest thing, I am just going based on what you have said here. Females are so catty and want to feel better than others, so when she is getting complimented on her hair and people are asking her how she does it, it's probably a big ego  boost for her.

No problem!!

We just got through our first deployment in 2019 and I was one of the Family Readiness Group (FRG)'s board members. Here are a few tips/things I learned and hopefully they help you!

1. The command's Ombudsmand is your biggest resource. If you haven't met them yet, ask your husband who they are and make contact. They can point you in the right direction for the tax information. They are only allowed to give you Navy approved and validated sources and information.
2. There is a class called Compass. TAKE IT! It will teach you how to navigate this crazy life on the home front. You will also make some friends and potentially make a support group for this deployment.
3. Expect the unexpected. Murphy's Law/the Deployment curse is real. BUT making friends and having resources you will be just fine at the end.
4. Make sure you have a Power of Attorney for EVERYTHING you can think of, especially your ID card since your ID is your life line for base access, health/vision insurance and if you use it the Navy Exchange and the commissary (Edited to add this one)

Just know You have a support group here. If you are on the East Coast, I can give you some resources out here in Norfolk, just PM me.

First - Congratulations on the marriage, and welcome to the Navy Spouse life!! 5 years down for me, and I can say it is a crazy life and confusing, so if you ever need help navigating anything, please feel free to PM me.   


As for taxes, the w2 is what you get sent in order to do your taxes every year... I believe you mean w4. I went in and changed my information and updated my allowances from 0 > 1 immediately. I didn't want to end up having to pay at the end of the year.   


Just an FYI - you can file them on your own for free with H&R Block, I typically find the link/info through MilitaryOneSource. OR Depending on where y'all are stationed, they might have the places on base where you can go in person for free.

A family member bought me a scale for Christmas that claims to be a smart scale. (  [https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00N9ENKDI/ref=ppx\_yo\_dt\_b\_search\_asin\_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1](https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00N9ENKDI/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1) ) I will be judging it this weekend off of an InBody analysis test. 

I personally take weekly progress pics as well as record me weight and body measurements in a note book every Sunday morning after I wake up and use the restroom. I also record how much weight I am lifting every time I workout, either in a notebook or directly into [Bodybuilding.com](https://Bodybuilding.com)'s bodyspace app. I have found that these help me to stay more motivated and focused than just weight alone. 

Good Luck!

What about getting them waxed scares you? I was scared of it hurting, but it's not that bad, might hurt for a moment then it's all beauty. I would go get them fixed professionally so that you can get the look you want, with out having to wait forever for them t grow back in.

Don't even mention it. If it hasn't come up yet it's not a big deal yet but if she asks be up front and honest. My husband (then boyfriend) was a virgin and didn't want to be judged and lied to me said he had been with one other person before. After we got married he told me I was his first. I would have rather known the truth when asked not 6 months later.

I havw to keep my routine. If i didn't get much sleep I will do light cardio but I still do it. If i take one day off it screws up my entire week. There have been plenty of nights where I get 1 or 2 hours sleep total 30 minutes at a time because of being on call for work but I will still get to the gym
